message.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Recently it has been proposed that the consistency with T-duality requires the effective action of string theory at order <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$\alpha '^n$$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:msup>
                    <mml:mi>α</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mrow>
                      <mml:mo>′</mml:mo>
                      <mml:mi>n</mml:mi>
                    </mml:mrow>
                  </mml:msup>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> to satisfy the least action principle provided that the values of the massless fields and their derivatives up to order <jats:italic>n</jats:italic> are known on the boundary. In this paper we speculate that this boundary condition constrains the field redefinitions and the corrections to the T-duality transformations in the presence of boundary, e.g., at order <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$\alpha '$$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:msup>
                    <mml:mi>α</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mo>′</mml:mo>
                  </mml:msup>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>, the metric does not change, and all other massless fields should change to include only the first derivative of the massless fields. Using the above restricted field redefinitions, we write all gauge invariant bulk and boundary couplings in the bosonic string theory at order <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$\alpha '$$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:msup>
                    <mml:mi>α</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mo>′</mml:mo>
                  </mml:msup>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> in a minimal scheme. Then using the assumption that the effective action of string theory at the critical dimension is background independent, we fix the coefficients of the tree-level gauge invariant couplings by imposing <jats:italic>O</jats:italic>(1, 1) symmetry when the background has a circle and by imposing <jats:italic>O</jats:italic>(<jats:italic>d</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>d</jats:italic>) symmetry when the background has <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$T^d$$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:msup>
                    <mml:mi>T</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mi>d</mml:mi>
                  </mml:msup>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>. These constraints fix the bulk action up to an overall factor, and the boundary action up to two parameters. By requiring the gravity couplings in the boundary action to be consistent with those in the Chern-Simons gravity, the two boundary parameters are also fixed. Up to a restricted field redefinition, the bulk and boundary couplings are exactly those in the K.A. Meissner action and its corresponding boundary action.</jats:p>
title: Higher-derivative field redefinitions in the presence of boundary
